q: Is the paper's claim that each 'custom' C[[i,j]],k gate (Appendix A) costs the same 7 laser pulses as a standard Toffoli exactly true, or does it hide a phase-tracking overhead that a fair modern pulse-level noise model would surface? Reproducing the 4-pulse saving from EXP N (Eq. 7.5) to EXP N' (Eq. 7.9) at the pulse level would settle whether the '38 laser pulses' headline is robust or a bookkeeping artifact.
basis: The abstract's headline number (38 pulses) uses EXP N' (Eq. 7.9) rather than the EXP N (Eq. 7.5) we directly simulated. We verified that EXP N takes 34 pulses (matching Eq. 7.6 exactly), so the 4-pulse gap is entirely absorbed by the custom-gate accounting in Appendix A, which we did not independently pulse-decompose.
next_steps: Implement the Appendix A pulse decompositions for C[[i,j]],k (the four combinations of control values) in QuTiP or a Cirac-Zoller simulator (Molmer-Sorensen + carrier pulses); compare the fidelity-adjusted pulse cost against a standard Toffoli. If they differ, redo the '38 pulses to factor 15' arithmetic.

q: At what per-pulse depolarizing/dephasing error rate p does the full 38-pulse 'factor 15' demo succeed with probability >= 1/2 end-to-end? The paper is purely coherent and never asks this, but for the mid-1990s ion-trap fidelities the answer is what actually determined whether the demo was buildable.
basis: Our replication only ran ideal statevector simulation (fidelity = 1.000, uniform y distribution). Adding a depolarizing noise model to Qiskit Aer and sweeping p in [1e-4, 1e-1] on the same 6-qubit circuit is a finite, tractable extension that would produce a paper-relevant number the original never computed.
next_steps: Rerun the 6-qubit circuit with qiskit_aer's noise model over Toffoli-decomposed CX+H+T gates for a sweep of two-qubit gate error p; extract the empirical success probability of recovering r=4 from the QFT samples. Compare against per-pulse ion-trap fidelities from Wineland/Blatt-era papers (1996-2001).

q: How much of the 1996 quantum-circuits literature that writes operators in 'algebraic' right-to-left form (as in Eq. 7.5 here) is silently ambiguous, and how many independent replications have gotten the ordering wrong? Our replication only worked once we applied the rightmost operator first, matching the paper's Sec. VI ADD convention (Eq. 6.36) but never stated explicitly in Sec. VII.
basis: During implementation we had to make a specific choice: left-to-right (as read on the page) vs. right-to-left (standard operator-product acting on a ket). We chose right-to-left based on consistency with the ADD sequences and confirmed correctness against the lookup table. A wrong choice would have flipped which basis state each Toffoli 'corrects' and produced a scrambled output.
next_steps: Survey a sample of quant-ph submissions from 1994-2000 with explicit small-N circuits, and check whether authors state the convention. Would inform good replication practice for pre-Nielsen-Chuang circuit notation.

q: What is the smallest N for which no analogous hand-crafted single-Toffoli-layer EXP N circuit exists (i.e., where the trick of 'x^{2^L} \equiv 1 mod N for all coprime x' fails)? For N=15 the trick collapses because Carmichael(15)=4, so L=2 suffices; for N=21 lambda(21)=6, N=33 lambda(33)=10, etc. When does the specialized shortcut lose to the 72 K^3 general-purpose construction?
basis: Section VII exploits x^4 \equiv 1 mod 15 for all coprime x, which lets L=2 replace the general L=2K=8 and lets EXP N be a table of only 4 rows. This trick is very fragile in N.
next_steps: For each odd composite N in [15, 100], compute Carmichael(N) and the minimum L needed for r | 2^L to hold for at least half of coprime x; count Toffolis needed for the 2^L-row lookup table. Tabulate specialized vs. general-purpose pulse counts and identify the crossover.

q: Can the Section VII '15,284 pulses on 21 qubits' and '14,878 pulses on 22 qubits' general-purpose figures for N=15 be reproduced from a modern re-derivation? The paper does not release code, and these are the numbers that anchor the abstract's 396 K^3 headline; nobody appears to have re-derived them in the ~30 years since.
basis: We fully replicated the specialized N=15 construction of Sec. VII but did not exercise the general-purpose K=4, L=8 cascade that produces the 15,284-pulse estimate. That estimate is the empirical anchor tying the K=4 case to the paper's asymptotic 396 K^3 claim, so an independent count matters.
next_steps: Implement (in Qiskit or a symbolic circuit synthesizer) the paper's ADD, MUXADD, MULT, MODMULT, and EXP N routines from Sec. V-VI at K=4, L=8; count NOTs, CNOTs, Toffolis symbolically; convert to Cirac-Zoller pulses; compare against 15,284 and 14,878. Also test whether the +1-qubit optimization giving 14,878 is stable to different design choices.
